SMTO-FIL-0033 — The receiving Gateway didn't confirm the copied data correctly

GUID: c9345598-839e-46c7-9dc3-e1fb2473ffb0
Slug: file-invalid-destination-receipt
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • While copying a file between Gateways, the receiving computer reported a different amount of data than SMTO had just sent. SMTO stopped the copy before putting the file in place at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, check that both Gateways are connected, and use Check for updates on each one. A Gateway on an older version or with an unsteady connection can report copy progress incorrectly.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  3. If the destination file is missing or still the old version, ask SMTO to copy it again. SMTO stopped before finishing, so a fresh copy is needed once you've confirmed it isn't there.

What success looks like

  • The new copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't delete files in the destination folder yourself; leave any file whose name starts with .smto-transfer- (it may be hidden) for them to check.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • During a Gateway copy, a destination_write reply reported bytes_received different from the offset the controller had just written up to, so the relay stopped and aborted the stage before destination_commit.

What this means

  • A destination_write reply reports bytes_received different from the next offset the controller just sent. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A destination_write reply reports bytes_received different from the next offset the controller just sent.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the original session's acknowledged offset with the sent chunk and cleanup/recovery state.

How to fix it

  • Compare destination_status for the transfer_id with the source size, and check both Gateways' logs and versions for a transfer-protocol mismatch or a restarted session. The relay aborted before destination_commit, so the destination path was not published; confirm the .smto-transfer-*.partial stage was removed (cleanup_complete) before starting a new copy, and never resend individual chunks.
  • Inspect and reconcile the original transfer acknowledgement and staging state; do not blindly resend the chunk.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original transfer is settled with verified byte accounting before further work.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
